topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the cancer lecture series, outlines the course structure, and defines the learning objectives concerning cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Intrinsic Errors versus Environmental Risk Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the fundamental biology of cancer development while weighing the relative contributions of random endogenous mutations against environmental exposures.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms by which infectious agents cause cancer, focusing on Epstein-Barr virus and the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how various physical and chemical mutagens undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts, transversions, and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and Host Susceptibility Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how non-mutagenic tumor promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and host developmental timing facilitate malignant transformation.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify carcinogens and evaluate cancer risk.
